_format: Branching conversation flow for the Conversation Builder. Nodes are steps; each has lines you can say (`say`), what the person may answer (`responses`) and where each answer leads (`next`). `{{...}}` slots are filled from the chosen subject and statement. Lines without `chk` are machine translated by scripts/fill_conversation_phrases.py and flagged until someone corrects them. `lessons` lists the Love People lessons whose quoted lines are offered as extra options at that step.

the-future.en: Do you think the world will ever become a better place?
Many people worry about the future. Does it worry you too?

family.en: What do you think helps a family to stay happy?
Raising children is not easy today. Where do you think parents can find good advice?

god.en: Do you think it is possible to really know God?
Have you ever wondered whether God has a personal name?

prayer.en: Do you think God listens when we pray?
Some people feel their prayers are not heard. Have you ever felt that way?

jesus.en: Why do you think Jesus is still so well known today?
Do you think the advice Jesus gave still works in our time?

god-s-kingdom.en: Many people pray for God's Kingdom to come. What do you think that Kingdom is?
Do you think any government can solve the problems people face today?

suffering.en: Why do you think there is so much suffering in the world?
Do you think God cares when people suffer?

death.en: Do you think we will ever see our loved ones who have died again?
What do you think happens to us when we die?

religion.en: Do you think all religions are acceptable to God?
There are so many religions. How do you think a person can find the true one?

guidance.en: Start with the person, not your subject. Notice what they are doing and speak naturally, as you would to a friend. (Love People, lessons 1 and 2)

think.en: What is the person doing right now? What might they be thinking about?
Is this a good time to talk to this person?

say.en: Hello! How are you today?
Good morning. My name is {{me}}. What is your name?
It is good to see you. Do you have a few minutes to talk?
I noticed you are busy with your children. They are beautiful.

they.en: I am fine, thank you. And you?
I am sorry, I do not have time right now.
I am not interested, thank you.

title.en: Raise the subject with a question

guidance.en: Ask a question the person can have an opinion about, then listen. Do not correct them yet; you are learning what they think. (Lessons 1, 2 and 9)

they.en: Yes, I have thought about that.
I am not sure. What do you think?

label.en: They disagree or hold a different belief

they.en: No, I do not believe that.
My church teaches something different.
Why does God allow it, then?
I do not know. Nobody really knows.

guidance.en: Acknowledge what they said, then offer one verse, not a sermon. Keep it short and simple. (Lessons 3 and 11)

say.en: Thank you for sharing that. Many people feel the same way.
The Bible gives a comforting answer to that. May I show you one short verse?
That is an interesting view. May I read you what the Bible says about it?
I would like to show you one verse. It will take only a minute.

they.en: All right, go ahead.
No, I do not want to read the Bible right now.
I really must go now.

title.en: State the truth and read the scripture

guidance.en: Say the Bible truth in one sentence, read the verse, then ask what they think. Let the verse do the teaching. (Truths We Love to Teach; lesson 11)

say.en: Let us read {{scripture}}. Would you like to read it, or shall I?
Notice what this verse says.
What do you think this means?
How do you feel about that promise?

they.en: That is beautiful. I did not know the Bible said that.
I do not think that is what it means.
But when will that happen?
Hmm. I have to think about that.

title.en: Make it clear with a question or illustration

guidance.en: Give them time. Use a simple question or a picture from daily life to make the point clear, then return to the verse. (Lessons 8 and 11)

say.en: Think of it this way. When a father promises his child something good, does the child doubt it?
God made this promise, and God cannot lie.
May I ask, what part is hard to accept?

they.en: I see what you mean.
I still do not think so.

guidance.en: Commend the question, show you understand the feeling behind it, and answer from the Bible. If it leads away from the subject, offer to come back to it. (Lessons 9 and 5)

say.en: That is a very good question. Many people ask it.
I understand why you feel that way.
The Bible answers that. May I show you?
That is a big question. May I come back and answer it properly next time?

they.en: Yes, please.
All right, you can come back.
No, that is enough for today.

title.en: When they disagree: stay calm and kind

guidance.en: Do not argue. Find something to agree with, ask why they believe it, and offer the Bible's view only if they are willing. A calm manner teaches more than winning a point. (Lessons 5 and 12; Should You End the Conversation?)

say.en: I respect your belief. May I ask why you believe that?
You are right that many people believe that.
I am not here to argue. I only want to share what I found in the Bible.
Would you be willing to look at one verse and tell me what you think?

they.en: All right, show me the verse.
I have my own beliefs, thank you.
I do not want to talk about religion.

guidance.en: Build on their interest: share a second truth on the same subject, or offer a free Bible lesson. Decide together on the next step. (Lessons 7 and 10)

say.en: There is more the Bible says about this. Would you like to learn more?
We have a free Bible course that answers questions like this. Would you like to try one lesson?
You can also find this on jw.org in Chuukese.

they.en: Yes, I would like that.
Not now, but thank you.

guidance.en: Respect their time. Leave one thought and ask for a better time. (Lessons 3 and 7)

say.en: I can see you are busy. I will not keep you.
May I come back another time? When would be good for you?
Before I go, may I leave you with one short thought?

they.en: Yes, come back on Saturday morning.
No, please do not come back.

label.en: They will listen for a moment

they.en: All right, but only a minute.

guidance.en: One sentence of hope and one question to think about. Short is powerful. (Lesson 11)

say.en: I will leave you with this thought: {{statement}}
You can read more about it at {{scripture}} when you have time.
Think about it, and next time tell me what you concluded.

label.en: They accept and are open to another visit

they.en: Thank you. I will think about it.
All right. Goodbye.

guidance.en: Agree on a day and time, say what you will talk about, and leave a question to think about. Keep your word. (Lesson 10)

say.en: When would be a good time for me to come back?
Next time we can look at this question: {{next_question}}
May I have your phone number so I can let you know before I come?
I will see you on {{day}} then. Thank you for your time.

they.en: Saturday morning is fine.
I do not know. Maybe another time.

guidance.en: Stay kind. Thank them, leave on good terms, and leave the door open. How you leave is what they will remember. (Lesson 3; Should You End the Conversation?)

say.en: I understand. Thank you for your time.
I am sorry to have disturbed you. Have a good day.
If you ever have a question about the Bible, you can find answers at jw.org in Chuukese.
May I leave you with just one thought before I go?

they.en: All right, one thought.
No, thank you. Goodbye.

guidance.en: Thank them, repeat the main point in one sentence, and say goodbye warmly. (Lessons 3 and 10)

say.en: Thank you for talking with me today.
I enjoyed our conversation. Remember: {{statement}}
May God bless you and your family. Goodbye.
I hope we can talk again.

they.en: Thank you. Goodbye.

guidance.en: Afterwards, note what they said and what you will bring next time.
